Voaters who ride motorcycles, what are some good brands/styles of backpacks to use while riding?
I have a black bugout backpack that I got in the army, looks like this: link
I haven't ridden in a while and used a simple jansport when I did, but if I had bought another I would have looked for a waterproof one. I got caught by rain a few times.

Yes! He's told me he's been caught in the rain a couple of times. We also live in the middle of nowhere and have those field sprinklers that'll spray into the road sometimes.

Ditch the backpack altogether. I've ridden for over 30 years now, on all kinds of bikes, and regularly commute 20 miles on a bike. Backpacks are uncomfortable, hot, and somewhat dangerous. I've been in far too many situations when a crosswind has pushed me further than it should have because of my backpack. Or maybe the weight of the pack has caused me to ride uncomfortably.

Just try out either a tank bag or a tail bag. Really. Just try it. Lowering the weight and getting it off your back will make a world of difference.

I know this isn't what you wanted to read. And I hope I'm not coming off like a pompous ass. But please just try it. I use tail bags most of the time now and I'll never go back.

My regular commuter bike is a Triumph Daytona 955i and I have a Ventura rack on the back. I strap a pack to that rack and it works well. When I'm feeling old (or want to go really fast), I ride a BMW K1200RS with a factory rack and pack on the tail. It works well.

Just try it. Maybe get a tail bag and put it on the rear seat. The sense of freedom is a great thing. Free yourself from the backpack.

This is totally what I wanted to read. I hardly know anything about motorcycles so any extra information helps. I'm so glad you suggested something other than a backpack. I would have never known to look at anything other than a that. I'd rather him be safe than anything else. Thank you!!

Honestly never thought about a brand. I usually just get get a smallish, comfortable black one.

I've been riding 25 years. A backpack is okay for short distances, but not for long trips. It puts a lot of stress on your back, especially if you are riding a superbike. Also raises your centre of gravity. Rather get a tankbag, saddlebag, panniers or a top box.
Ah! Thank you! He's a tall guy and I understand the whole center gravity stuff. So I'm definitely looking into other options now especially after reading other comments.

I use a Chrome messenger bag like this one.

http://www.chromeindustries.com/us/en/bags/messenger-bags/citizen-messenger-bag

The advantage is, when adjusted properly, the conform to your body, and unless you're carrying something stupid that's super heavy and super small like a cannonball or something, the bag never shifts weight. With other bags, on sharp turns it'll pull on me and I'll have to adjust my balance, but this is more like just having a heavier torso.

I used to recommend condor bags for the super comfortable shoulder straps, but my last one melted from being sat too close to the exhaust. I have been using a sandpiper of California (S.O.C.) bag I bought when I was in the Army. I have yet to be able to break/rip/otherwise ruin this bag.

Reference: http://www.amazon.com/Sandpiper-California-Three-Pass-Backpack/dp/B007VMOU92

I use it to haul 50lbs of books to and from class everyday as well. They make awesome bags with places to tie stuff, tons of pockets, and they come with strong cord pulls on the zippers. You can loop them through eachother a few times to make sure the zippers don't fall open on a long ride, but you can still undue them with one hand. My vote goes to a Sandpiper bag, as I have managed to destroy every other pack I have owned haha.
